posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
That looks odd, because the default settings should have them much lower than that.
But regardless, each row has a plugin parameter for Home X and Home Y. They're even fairly straightforward, so looking at the default for Row 1 Home X:
Code:
maxRowX - (maxRows - rowId) * 112 + rowIndex * 32
maxRowX you defined above, the Maximum Row X plugin parameter
maxRows, again, defined above the Maximum Rows
rowId, simply, is which row you're looking at
rowIndex is which member in the row this actor is, starting with 0.
So in your first screenshot above, the actor with the glasses is in rowId 2 and rowIndex 0.
Thus, we can see that the first chunk of the formula is determining where the actor rows start and the space between them, and you would change that by changing the 112 (and/or maxRowX). Then the second half is controlling the diagonal slant as you add actors to the row, and you would change that by changing the 32.
The Home Y formula works exactly the same way.
